marta: Heads-up — on bringup of q4-reranker-int4 we're seeing NDCG up ~1% but MRR down ~1.7% vs fp32. noise concentrated by query length, short queries worst. dumping quick bucketed stats below.
omar: Can you paste the eval command + config you ran?
marta: ```
./eval_harness --model q4-reranker-int4 \n  --holdout release_v3 \n  --metrics ndcg@10,mrr@10,ndcg@1 \n  --sampling stratified --strata-by length:percentiles=25,50,75 \
  --candidate-normalization=loglen
```
kevin: My first guess: quantization changed softmax sharpness / numeric stability. MRR (top1) is very sensitive. Try simple temperature scaling on logits per-length-bucket.
sree: Also verify tokenization/whitespace normalization. We had an earlier case where stray HTML/meta changed short-query winners. Any signs of holdout leakage?
marta: Quick bucketed numbers from the smoke run (fp32 -> int4):
  short (<20 toks): ndcg@10 +0.3%, mrr@10 -2.4%
  mid (20-80): ndcg@10 +1.1%, mrr@10 -0.2%
  long (>80): ndcg@10 +0.4%, mrr@10 +0.6%
So the hit is concentrated in short queries (top1 swaps).
omar: That pattern screams a tiny arithmetic change in normalization or epsilon handling. For short candidates denominator small -> larger relative effect. Is candidate-normalization code identical between runtimes?
marta: I diffed the ranking code. Normalization exists but the fastpath in the quant runtime uses a different epsilon. Snippet from logs:
  fp32: "score_norm = score / (len_tokens + 1e-12)"
  q4 runtime: "score_norm = score / (len_tokens + 1e-6)"
That 1e-6 vs 1e-12 matters when len_tokens is 1-3.
kevin: Yep. For short queries that will shift logits by ~1e-6 scale -> after softmax top1 can flip. Quick mitigation: apply temperature scaling per-short-bucket. Try temp=1.2 and re-eval.
marta: Ran temp=1.2 only for short bucket (local). New delta: short mrr improved from -2.4 -> -0.6. Not fully recovered but much better.
sree: Longer term: align epsilons and add a unit test for len=1/2/3 candidate sets. Also add a per-bucket calibration fallback flag in runtime config so we can patch behavior without full release.
omar: Also compute pairwise win-rate against fp32 for top1 on short queries. If pairwise win-rate for gold decreases widely, it's real regression. If only marginal, could be noise.
marta: Pairwise top1 win-rate among short queries: gold chosen by fp32 in 1000 cases; q4 picks same in 962 cases -> 38 swaps (3.8%). Most swaps are between two near-equal candidates.
kevin: That aligns with epsilon artifact. Small noise causing swap. Plan: (A) push epsilon fix (B) add per-length temp fallback (C) add len=short unit test and sample-case in regression harness (D) run full release_v3 holdout overnight.
marta: Pushed quick patch to match epsilon. Re-ran local smoke: short mrr now -0.5 (acceptable margin). Kicking full eval job.
deploy-bot: Rerank-eval job queued: run-987654321 (ETA ~6h) :hourglass_flowing_sand: 
omar: After full eval, if short bucket still worse >1% we block canary and apply per-length temperature as a mitigation. Otherwise ship.
sree: Also add a short-query slice to the rollout checklist and a note in the release PR summarizing the epsilon cause.
marta: Will open PR with unit test + bake plan + cherry-pick for stable branch. Thanks all :thumbsup:
